These can be used as fixed values for the lens light and mass models in a model-fit.

The emission from these images will impact our model fitting and needs to be removed from the analysis.

- [Data Preparation: PSF](scripts/imaging/data_preparation/examples/psf.py): The Point Spread Function (PSF) describes blurring due the optics of your dataset`s telescope. It is used by PyAutoLens when fitting a dataset to include these effects, such that does not bias the model.

- [SLaM (Source, Light and Mass): DSPL](scripts/imaging/features/advanced/double_source_plane_lens/slam.py): This script adapts the SLaM (Source, Light and Mass) pipelines to a Double Source Plane Lens (DSPL) system, where there are two source galaxies at different redshifts behind the lens galaxy. Both source galaxies must be modeled simultaneously because the first source (at the intermediate redshift) acts as both a background source of the lens galaxy and as an additional deflector for the second (higher-redshift) source.

- [Features: Mass Stellar Dark Fit](scripts/imaging/features/advanced/mass_stellar_dark/fit.py): A decomposed mass model splits the lens galaxy's total mass into a stellar component (tied to its observed light via a mass-to-light ratio) and a dark matter component (typically an NFW halo). The total deflection at every image-plane coordinate is the sum of the deflections produced by each component, plus any external shear.
  - Contents: Prerequisites, Dataset & Mask, Over Sampling, MGE Basis, Galaxies, Tracer, Fit, Decomposed Deflection, Intensities, Wrap Up

- [Potential Correction: Start Here](scripts/imaging/features/advanced/potential_correction/start_here.py): Parametric lens mass models (e.g. the `PowerLaw` used throughout the workspace) are smooth: their convergence and deflection angles vary gradually across the image plane. Real lens galaxies are not perfectly smooth. They contain substructure — dark matter subhaloes, globular clusters, satellite galaxies — and their large-scale mass distributions can depart from ellipsoidal symmetry in ways no simple parametric profile captures.
  - Contents: Simulate, Smooth Model Fit, Joint Fit, Dkappa Map, Iterative Fit, Evidence Sampling
- [Modeling Features: Shapelets](scripts/imaging/features/advanced/shapelets/fit.py): A shapelet is a basis function that is appropriate for capturing the exponential / disk-like features of a galaxy. It has been employed in many strong lensing studies to model the light of the lensed source galaxy, because it can represent features of disky star forming galaxies that a single Sersic function cannot.

- [Modeling Features: Linear Light Profiles Fit](scripts/imaging/features/linear_light_profiles/fit.py): A "linear light profile" is a variant of a standard light profile where the `intensity` parameter is solved for via linear algebra every time the model is fitted to the data. This uses a process called an "inversion" and it always computes the `intensity` values that give the best fit to the data (e.g. maximize the likelihood) given the light profile's other parameters.
  - Contents: Advantages & Disadvantages, Positive Only Solver, Model, Notes, Dataset & Mask, Over Sampling, Fit, Intensities, Visualization, Wrap Up

  - Contents: Simplifications, Prerequisites, Dataset & Mask, Over Sampling, Masked Image Grid, Mesh Shape, Edge Zeroing, Lens Galaxy, Source Galaxy Pixelization and Regularization, Lens Light, Ray Tracing, Border Relocation, Source Pixel Centre Calculation, Interpolation, Mapper, Alternative Meshes, Mapping Matrix, Image Reconstruction, Likelihood Function, Chi Squared, Regularization Term, Complexity Terms, Noise Normalization Term, Calculate The Log Likelihood, Fit, Lens Modeling, Wrap Up
- [Features: Pixelization Modeling](scripts/imaging/features/pixelization/modeling.py): A pixelization reconstructs the source's light using a pixel-grid, which is regularized using a prior that forces the solution to have a degree of smoothness.
  - Contents: GPU Run Times, CPU Users, Advantages & Disadvantages, Positive Only Solver, Model, Dataset & Mask, Over Sampling, Mesh Shape, Edge Zeroing, Search, Position Likelihood, Brief Description, Analysis, VRAM, Run Time, Result, Mask Extra Galaxies, Wrap Up, Chaining, HowToGalaxy
- [Plots: Pixelization](scripts/imaging/features/pixelization/plot.py): This example illustrates how to plot fits which reconstruct the source galaxy using a pixelization.
  - Contents: Setup, Fit Imaging, Inversion, Mapper Grids, Mapper Galaxy Dict, Fit Interferometer
- [Pixelization: SLaM](scripts/imaging/features/pixelization/slam.py): This script provides an example of the Source, (Lens) Light, and Mass (SLaM) pipelines for pixelized source modeling.
  - Contents: Prerequisites, SOURCE LP PIPELINE, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 1, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 2, LIGHT LP PIPELINE, MASS TOTAL PIPELINE, Dataset, Settings AutoFit, Redshifts, Mesh Shape, SLaM Pipeline
- [Pixelization: Source Science](scripts/imaging/features/pixelization/source_science.py): Source science focuses on studying the highly magnified properties of the background lensed source galaxy (or galaxies).
  - Contents: Model Fit, Interpolated Source, Source Flux, Zoom, Errors, Magnification, Masking, Magnification via Mesh, Reconstruction CSV
- [Features: Scaling Relation Fit](scripts/imaging/features/scaling_relation/fit.py): Fits the `scaling_relation` dataset with every parameter set to the simulator's truth, so the two-tier foreground population can be inspected without a non-linear search in the way.
  - Contents: Dataset & Mask, Centres + Luminosities, Over Sampling, The Relation, Galaxies, Tracer & Fit, The Relation, Evaluated, Deflection Sum, Intensities, CSV Interface, Wrap Up.
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Scaling Relation__](scripts/imaging/features/scaling_relation/likelihood_function.py): Describes the one step of the `log_likelihood` computation that a scaling relation changes: how the lens plane's deflection field is composed when most of the foreground galaxies' Einstein radii are not free parameters but derived from the main lens's.
  - Contents: Dataset & Mask, Centres + Luminosities, The Relation, Galaxies, Per-Galaxy Deflection, Manual Ray-Tracing, Source-Plane Image, Likelihood, CSV Interface, Wrap Up.
- [Modeling Features: Scaling Relation](scripts/imaging/features/scaling_relation/modeling.py): A strong lens often has many foreground galaxies near the line of sight, and freeing an `einstein_radius` for each one quickly stops working: with 30 companions the parameter space is too large to sample and the data does not contain enough information to constrain them individually anyway.
  - Contents: Dataset & Mask, Centres, Luminosities, Over Sampling, Main Lens & Source, Bounded Tier, Scaling Tier, Model, Zero Free Parameters, Search / Analysis / Fit / Result., CSV Interface, Wrap Up.
- [Simulator: Scaling Relation](scripts/imaging/features/scaling_relation/simulator.py): Simulates the dataset for the `imaging/features/scaling_relation` feature: a galaxy-scale lens plus two tiers of foreground companions.
  - Contents: Dataset Paths / Grid / PSF / Simulator, Luminosity Convention, Main Lens Galaxy, Faber-Jackson Relation, Bounded Companions, Scaling Companions, Source / Dataset / Records
- [Scaling Relation: SLaM](scripts/imaging/features/scaling_relation/slam.py): Uses the SLaM pipelines to fit a lens with two tiers of foreground companions, where the scaling tier's Einstein radii are tied to the main lens's own Einstein radius by a Faber-Jackson relation.
  - Contents: Luminosity Measurement, LENS LIGHT PIPELINE, SOURCE LP PIPELINE, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 1 / 2, LIGHT LP PIPELINE, MASS TOTAL PIPELINE, Dataset / Centres / Settings / Redshifts / Mesh Shape., SLaM Pipeline, Measured Luminosities
- [Simulator: Manual Signal to Noise Ratio](scripts/imaging/features/simulator_manual_signal_to_noise_ratio.py): When simulating `Imaging` of a strong lens, one is often not concerned with the actual units of the light (e.g. electrons per second, counts, etc.) but instead simple wants the data to correspond to a certain signal to noise value.
  - Contents: Model, Dataset Paths, Simulate, Ray Tracing, Output, Visualize, Tracer json
- [Fits](scripts/imaging/fit.py): This guide shows how to fit data using the `FitImaging` object, including visualizing and interpreting its results.
  - Contents: Loading Data, Mask, Fitting, Bad Fit, Fit Quantities, Figures of Merit, Plane Quantities, Unmasked Quantities, Pixel Counting, Outputting Results
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Inversion (Parametric)__](scripts/imaging/likelihood_function.py): This script provides a step-by-step guide of the `log_likelihood_function` which is used to fit `Imaging` data with a lens light profile and source light profile (e.g. an elliptical Sersic lens and source).
  - Contents: JAX, Dataset & Mask, Over Sampling, Masked Image Grid, Lens Galaxy Mass, Lens Galaxy, Source Galaxy Light Profile, Lens Light, Ray Tracing, Source Image, Convolution, Likelihood Function, Chi Squared, Noise Normalization Term, Calculate The Log Likelihood, Fit, Lens Modeling, Wrap Up
- [Imaging: Modeling](scripts/imaging/modeling.py): This script is the starting point for lens modeling of CCD imaging data (E.g. Hubble Space Telescope, Euclid) with **PyAutoLens** and it provides an overview of the lens modeling API.
  - Contents: Model, Plotters, Simulation, Data Preparation, Dataset & Mask, Extra Galaxies Noise Scaling, Over Sampling, Model Composition, Coordinates, Improved Lens Model, Linear Light Profiles, Concise API, Search, Unique Identifier, Iterations Per Update, Live Visual Update, Analysis, JAX, VRAM Use, Run Times, Output Folder Layout, Result, Features, HowToLens, Modeling Customization
- [Plots: Imaging](scripts/imaging/plot.py): This example shows how to plot an `Imaging` dataset and a `FitImaging` fit, figure by figure and via multi-panel subplots.
  - Contents: Dataset, Dataset Figures, Dataset Subplot, Fit, Fit Figures, Plane Images, Plane Subplots, Fit Subplot, Fit Subplot (Log10), Tracer Subplot, Outputting to FITS, Visualizer
- [Simulator: Start Here](scripts/imaging/simulator.py): This script is the starting point for simulating galaxy-galaxy strong lenses as CCD imaging data (E.g. Hubble Space Telescope, Euclid) and it provides an overview of the lens simulation API.
  - Contents: Model, Plotters, Dataset Paths, Grid, Over Sampling, PSF Convolution, Ray Tracing, Output, Visualize, Tracer json, Multiple Images, JAX Variant (Advanced), Oversampled PSF (Advanced)
- [Simulator: Sample](scripts/imaging/simulator_sample.py): This script illustrates how to simulate a sample of `Imaging` datasets of 'galaxy-scale' strong lenses, which can easily be used to simulate hundreds or thousands of strong lenses.
  - Contents: Model, Dataset Paths, Simulate, Sample Model Distributions, Sample Instances
- [Source Science](scripts/imaging/source_science.py): Source science focuses on studying the highly magnified properties of the background lensed source galaxy (or galaxies).
  - Contents: Simulated Dataset, Mask, Source Values, Source Flux, Source Magnification, Tracer, Parametric Source Models
- [Start Here: Imaging](scripts/imaging/start_here.py): Strong gravitational lenses are often observed with CCD imaging, for example using HST, JWST, or ground-based telescopes.
  - Contents: JAX, Google Colab Setup, Imports, Dataset, Extra Galaxy Removal, Masking, Model, Model Fit, Iterations Per Update, Live Visual Update, Result, Extra Galaxy Removal GUI, Model Your Own Lens, Simulator, Sample, Wrap Up

## group

- [Group: Data Preparation](scripts/group/data_preparation/start_here.py): When a group-scale strong lens CCD imaging dataset is analysed, it must conform to certain standards in order for the analysis to be performed correctly. This tutorial describes these standards and links to more detailed scripts which will help you prepare your dataset to adhere to them if it does not already.
  - Contents: Pixel Scale, Image, Noise Map, PSF, Data Processing Complete
- [Chaining: Group DSPL](scripts/group/features/advanced/double_source_plane_lens/chaining.py): This script chains two non-linear searches to fit `Imaging` data of a group-scale double source-plane lens (DSPL) — two source galaxies at different redshifts lensed by multiple main lens galaxies at the lens-plane redshift.
  - Contents: Dataset & Paths, Main Lens Centres, Masking (Search 1), Model (Search 1), Search + Result (Search 1), Masking (Search 2), Model (Search 2), Search + Result (Search 2), Wrap Up.
- [Features: Group DSPL Fit](scripts/group/features/advanced/double_source_plane_lens/fit.py): A group-scale double source-plane lens (DSPL), where two source galaxies at different redshifts are lensed by multiple main lens galaxies at the lens-plane redshift.
  - Contents: Prerequisites, Dataset, Mask, Over Sampling, Main Lens Centres, MGE Bases, Galaxies, Tracer, Fit, Multi-Plane Ray-Tracing, Wrap Up.
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Group DSPL__](scripts/group/features/advanced/double_source_plane_lens/likelihood_function.py): This script describes the additional steps required to compute the `log_likelihood` for a group-scale double source-plane lens (DSPL) — two source galaxies at different redshifts lensed by multiple main lens galaxies at the lens-plane redshift.
  - Contents: Prerequisites, Dataset & Mask, Main Lens Centres, Galaxies, Multi-Plane Ray-Tracing, Source-Plane Images, Likelihood, Fit Check, Wrap Up.
- [Modeling Features: Group DSPL](scripts/group/features/advanced/double_source_plane_lens/modeling.py): A group-scale double source-plane lens (DSPL), where two source galaxies at different redshifts are lensed by multiple main lens galaxies at the lens-plane redshift.
  - Contents: Model, Dataset, Mask, Over Sampling, Main Lens Centres, Model Composition, Cheating, Cosmology, Search, Analysis, Run-Time, Result, Wrap Up.
- [Simulator: Group DSPL](scripts/group/features/advanced/double_source_plane_lens/simulator.py): A double source-plane lens (DSPL) in a group-scale context, where two source galaxies at different redshifts are lensed by multiple main lens galaxies at the lens-plane redshift.
  - Contents: Dataset Paths, Grid, Galaxy Centres, Over Sampling, Main Lens Galaxies, Source Galaxies, Ray Tracing, Dataset, Tracer JSON, Centres JSON
- [SLaM (Source, Light and Mass): Group DSPL](scripts/group/features/advanced/double_source_plane_lens/slam.py): This script adapts the SLaM (Source, Light and Mass) pipelines to a group-scale Double Source Plane Lens (DSPL) system, where two source galaxies at different redshifts behind multiple main lens galaxies form a double Einstein ring.
- [Chaining: Group Mass Stellar Dark](scripts/group/features/advanced/mass_stellar_dark/chaining.py): This script chains two searches to fit `Imaging` data of a 'group-scale' strong lens where each main lens galaxy is decomposed into stellar + dark matter components.
  - Contents: Dataset + Masking, Main Lens Centres, Paths, Model (Search 1), Search 1, Model (Search 2), Search 2, Wrap Up
- [Features: Group Mass Stellar Dark Fit](scripts/group/features/advanced/mass_stellar_dark/fit.py): A group-scale strong lens where each main lens galaxy carries a decomposed mass model — a stellar component tied to its observed light via a mass-to-light ratio, plus a separately-parameterized dark matter halo. The total deflection at every image-plane coordinate is the sum over all main lens galaxies of the per-galaxy stellar + dark contributions, plus a single external shear.
  - Contents: Prerequisites, Dataset & Mask, Over Sampling, MGE Basis, Main Lens Centres, Galaxies, Tracer, Fit, Decomposed Deflection (Multi-Galaxy), Intensities, Wrap Up
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Group Mass Stellar Dark__](scripts/group/features/advanced/mass_stellar_dark/likelihood_function.py): This script describes the additional steps required to compute the `log_likelihood` for a group-scale strong lens whose mass model decomposes each main lens galaxy's mass into a stellar component (tied to its light via a mass-to-light ratio) and a separately-parameterized dark matter halo.
  - Contents: Prerequisites, Dataset & Mask, Main Lens Centres, Galaxies, Decomposed Deflection (Multi-Galaxy), Manual Ray-Tracing, Source-Plane Image, Model Image, Fit Check, Wrap Up.
- [Modeling Features: Group Mass Stellar Dark](scripts/group/features/advanced/mass_stellar_dark/modeling.py): A group-scale strong lens where each main lens galaxy carries a decomposed mass model: a stellar component tied to the galaxy's own light via a mass-to-light ratio, plus a separately-parameterized dark matter halo. The total lens-plane deflection is the sum, over every main lens galaxy, of stellar + dark contributions, plus a single external shear attached to `lens_0` representing the group-wide shear field.
  - Contents: Model, Dataset & Mask, Main Lens Centres, Over Sampling, Model Cookbook, Search, Analysis, VRAM, Run Time, Result, Wrap Up
- [Simulator: Group Mass Stellar Dark](scripts/group/features/advanced/mass_stellar_dark/simulator.py): A group-scale strong lens where each main lens galaxy carries a decomposed mass model: a stellar component tied to the galaxy's own light via a mass-to-light ratio, plus a separately-parameterized dark matter halo.
  - Contents: Dataset Paths, Grid, Galaxy Centres, Over Sampling, Main Lens Galaxies, Source Galaxy, Ray Tracing, Dataset, Tracer JSON, Centres JSON
- [SLaM (Source, Light and Mass): Group Mass Stellar Dark](scripts/group/features/advanced/mass_stellar_dark/slam.py): This script adapts the SLaM (Source, Light and Mass) pipelines to a group-scale strong lens where each main lens galaxy is decomposed into a stellar component (tied to its light via a mass-to-light ratio) and a dark matter halo.
- [Modeling Features: Operated Light Profiles (Group)](scripts/group/features/advanced/operated_light_profile/modeling.py): Operated light profiles are light profiles which are assumed to have already been convolved with the PSF. This means that during the model-fitting process, these profiles are NOT convolved again with the PSF, unlike standard light profiles.
  - Contents: Dataset & Mask, Centres, Over Sampling, Model, Search, Analysis, Result
- [Simulator: Operated Light Profiles (Group)](scripts/group/features/advanced/operated_light_profile/simulator.py): This script simulates a group-scale strong lens where the galaxy light uses operated light profiles. Operated light profiles represent emission that has already been convolved with the PSF, meaning they are NOT convolved again during the simulation.
  - Contents: Dataset Paths, Grid, Galaxy Centres, Over Sampling, Main Lens Galaxies, Extra Galaxies, Source Galaxy, Ray Tracing, Dataset, Centre JSON Files
- [Fit Features: Shapelets (Group)](scripts/group/features/advanced/shapelets/fit.py): A shapelet is a basis function that is appropriate for capturing the exponential / disk-like features of a galaxy. This script demonstrates how to create a fit using shapelet light profiles for a group-scale strong lens, without performing a non-linear search.
  - Contents: Dataset & Mask, Centres, Over Sampling, Basis, Fit, Intensities
- [Modeling Features: Shapelets (Group)](scripts/group/features/advanced/shapelets/modeling.py): A shapelet is a basis function that is appropriate for capturing the exponential / disk-like features of a galaxy. It has been employed in many strong lensing studies to model the light of lensed source galaxies, because it can represent features of disky star forming galaxies that a single Sersic function cannot.
  - Contents: Dataset & Mask, Centres, Over Sampling, Model, Search, Analysis, Result
- [Fit Features: Sky Background (Group)](scripts/group/features/advanced/sky_background/fit.py): The background of an image is the light that is not associated with the strong lens we are interested in. This script demonstrates how to include the sky background in a fit for a group-scale strong lens, without performing a non-linear search.
  - Contents: Dataset & Mask, Centres, Over Sampling, Fit
- [Modeling Features: Sky Background (Group)](scripts/group/features/advanced/sky_background/modeling.py): The background of an image is the light that is not associated with the strong lens we are interested in. This is due to light from the sky, zodiacal light, and light from other galaxies in the field of view.
  - Contents: Dataset & Mask, Centres, Over Sampling, Model, Search, Analysis, Result
- [Simulator: Sky Background (Group)](scripts/group/features/advanced/sky_background/simulator.py): This script simulates a group-scale strong lens dataset where the sky background is NOT subtracted from the image. The sky background is therefore present in the data and must be accounted for during model-fitting.
  - Contents: Dataset Paths, Grid, Galaxy Centres, Over Sampling, Main Lens Galaxies, Extra Galaxies, Source Galaxy, Ray Tracing, Dataset, Centre JSON Files
- [Subhalo Detection: Group](scripts/group/features/advanced/subhalo/detect/start_here.py): Strong gravitational lenses can be used to detect the presence of small-scale dark matter (DM) subhalos. This occurs when the DM subhalo overlaps the lensed source emission, and therefore gravitationally perturbs the observed image of the lensed source galaxy.
  - Contents: SLaM Pipelines, Grid Search, Group Adaptation, Dataset & Mask, Centres, Over Sampling, SLaM Pipeline Functions, Bayesian Evidence, Grid Search Result
- [Simulator: Subhalo (Group)](scripts/group/features/advanced/subhalo/simulator.py): If a low mass dark matter halo overlaps the lensed source emission, it perturbs it in a unique and observable way.
  - Contents: Dataset Paths, Grid, Galaxy Centres, Over Sampling, Main Lens Galaxies, Extra Galaxies, Source Galaxy, Ray Tracing, Dataset, Centre JSON Files, Subhalo Difference Image
- [Modeling Features (Group): The Group Halo — An Explicit Choice](scripts/group/features/group_halo/modeling.py): **Whether a group-scale lens model includes a separate dark-matter halo for the group is a modelling choice, not an assumption.** Some groups genuinely require one; others are adequately described by their member galaxies alone. This tutorial — the signature example of the group regime — fits the SAME dataset with both compositions and walks through how to decide between them:
  - Contents: Dataset, Model A, Model B, Fits, Model Comparison, Wrap Up
- [Simulator: Group Halo](scripts/group/features/group_halo/simulator.py): This script simulates the `Imaging` dataset fitted by the `group_halo` feature tutorial: a group-scale lens with a genuine **group-scale dark matter halo**, a brightest group galaxy (BGG) and two tidally truncated member galaxies, lensing a single extended background source.

  - Contents: Dataset & Mask, Galaxy Centres, Over Sampling, Fitting, Intensities, Visualization

- [Features: Group Scaling Relation Fit](scripts/group/features/scaling_relation/fit.py): A group-scale strong lens often has many foreground galaxies near the line of sight to the source, on top of one or more primary lens galaxies. The **three-tier API** splits these galaxies into populations that the lens model treats differently:
  - Contents: Prerequisites, Dataset & Mask, Centres + Luminosities, Over Sampling, MGE Basis, Galaxies, Tracer, Three-Tier Deflection Tour, Intensities, Wrap Up
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Group Scaling Relation__](scripts/group/features/scaling_relation/likelihood_function.py): This script describes the additional steps required to compute the `log_likelihood` for a group-scale strong lens whose foreground galaxy population is split across three tiers — main lens galaxies (modelled via the group `lens_dict` API), individually-modelled extras (each with its own free `einstein_radius`), and scaling-tier extras (whose Einstein radii are derived from a shared reference-anchored relation `einstein_radius = einstein_radius_ref * (luminosity / reference_luminosity) ** 0.5`, the Lenstool convention).
  - Contents: Prerequisites, Dataset & Mask., Centres + Luminosities, Galaxies, Three-Tier Deflection, Manual Ray-Tracing, Source-Plane Image, Fit Check., Wrap Up.
- [Modeling Features (Group): Scaling Relations](scripts/group/features/scaling_relation/modeling.py): Group-scale strong lenses can have many galaxies in the foreground beyond the primary lens. As the number grows, modelling each galaxy individually becomes impractical: a system with 10 companions would gain 10 extra Einstein-radius free parameters, and the data is rarely informative enough to constrain them all.
  - Contents: Three-Tier API, Centres, Luminosities, Dataset & Mask, Main Lens Galaxies, Extra Galaxies, Scaling Galaxies, Model, Over Sampling, Search and Analysis, Wrap Up
- [Modeling Features (Group): Fit Galaxy Luminosities for a Scaling Relation](scripts/group/features/scaling_relation/modeling_for_luminosities.py): The scaling-relation modeling examples (`modeling.py` in this directory and `scripts/imaging/features/scaling_relation/modeling.py`) need a measured **luminosity** for every galaxy that sits on the relation:
  - Contents: Dataset & Mask, Centres, Light-only Model, Search and Analysis, Compute Luminosities, Output, Wrap Up
- [Simulator: Group Scaling Relation](scripts/group/features/scaling_relation/simulator.py): This script simulates a group-scale strong lens with three populations of galaxies in the foreground, designed to exercise the three-tier modeling API used by `group/features/scaling_relation/modeling.py`:
- [Fits: Group](scripts/group/fit.py): This guide shows how to fit data using the `FitImaging` object for group-scale strong lenses, including visualizing and interpreting its results.
  - Contents: Loading Data, Mask, Galaxy Centres, Fitting, Bad Fit, Fit Quantities, Figures of Merit, Plane Quantities, Unmasked Quantities, Pixel Counting, Outputting Results, Over Sampling
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Group__](scripts/group/likelihood_function.py): This script provides a step-by-step guide of the `log_likelihood_function` which is used to fit `Imaging` data of a group-scale strong lens, where there are multiple lens galaxies whose mass profiles all contribute to the ray-tracing of the source galaxy.
  - Contents: JAX, Dataset & Mask, Over Sampling, Masked Image Grid, Main Lens Galaxy, Extra Galaxies, Source Galaxy Light Profile, Lens Light, Lens Galaxy Mass, Ray Tracing, Source Image, Convolution, Likelihood Function, Chi Squared, Noise Normalization Term, Calculate The Log Likelihood, Fit, Lens Modeling, Wrap Up
- [Group: Modeling](scripts/group/modeling.py): This script models an example strong lens on the 'group' scale, which typically have one or more "main" lens galaxies and smaller extra galaxies nearby, whose light may blur with the source light and whose mass contributes significantly to the ray-tracing, meaning both are therefore included in the strong lens model.
  - Contents: Scaling Relations, Group Halo, Example, Simulation, Data Preparation, Dataset & Mask, Main Galaxies and Extra Galaxies, Centres, Redshifts, Model, Coordinates, Improved Lens Model, Linear Light Profiles, Over Sampling, Search, Unique Identifier, Iterations Per Update, Live Visual Update, Analysis, JAX, VRAM Use, Run Times, Output Folder Layout, Result, Features, HowToLens, Modeling Customization
- [Plots: Group](scripts/group/plot.py): This example shows how to plot a group-scale `Imaging` dataset and a `FitImaging` fit, figure by figure and via multi-panel subplots.
  - Contents: Dataset, Dataset Figures, Dataset Subplot, Fit, Fit Figures, Plane Images, Fit Subplot, Visualizer
- [Simulator: Group](scripts/group/simulator.py): This script simulates an example strong lens on the 'group' scale, where there is a single primary lens galaxy and two smaller extra galaxies nearby, whose mass contributes significantly to the ray-tracing and is therefore included in the strong lens model.
  - Contents: Main Lens Galaxies vs Extra Galaxies, No Group Halo, Dataset Paths, Grid, Galaxy Centres, Over Sampling, PSF Convolution, Main Lens Galaxies, Extra Galaxies, Source Galaxy, Ray Tracing, Dataset, Visualize, Tracer json, Centre JSON Files
- [SLaM (Source, Light and Mass): Group Scale](scripts/group/slam.py): This script uses the SLaM pipelines to fit a group-scale strong lens, including extra galaxies and scaling galaxies surrounding the main lens whose light and mass are both modeled.
  - Contents: Prerequisites, Extra Galaxies and Scaling Galaxies, This Script, SOURCE LP PIPELINE 0, SOURCE LP PIPELINE 1, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 1, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 2, LIGHT LP PIPELINE, MASS TOTAL PIPELINE, Dataset, Galaxy Centres, Mask, Settings AutoFit, SLaM Pipeline
- [Source Science: Group](scripts/group/source_science.py): Source science focuses on studying the highly magnified properties of the background lensed source galaxy (or galaxies).
  - Contents: Simulated Dataset, Mask, Source Values, Source Flux, Source Magnification, Impact of Extra Galaxies, Tracer, Parametric Source Models
- [Start Here: Group](scripts/group/start_here.py): Group scale lenses typically have multiple lens galaxies whose light and mass all contribute significantly to the lensing of the source galaxy. Groups typically also have just one lensed source.
  - Contents: JAX, Google Colab Setup, Imports, Dataset, Main Lens Galaxies, Masking, Model, Model Fit, Live Visual Update, Result, Centre Input GUI, Model Your Own Lens, Wrap Up

## interferometer

- [Interferometer: CASA Reduction](scripts/interferometer/casa_reduction.py): This script is a practical walkthrough of how to reduce an ALMA / JVLA interferometer observation with **CASA** and export it into the three FITS files that **PyAutoLens** expects for lens modeling:
  - Contents: PyAutoLens Requirements, CASA in Five Steps, Step 1 — Split by Field / SPW, Step 2 — Channel Averaging, Step 3 — Continuum Subtraction, Step 4 — Rescale Sigmas, Step 5 — Export to FITS, Combining Spectral Windows, Polarisations, Building the Interferometer Object, Troubleshooting, SLACK
- [Interferometer: Data Preparation](scripts/interferometer/data_preparation.py): When an interferometer dataset is analysed, it must conform to certain standards in order for the analysis to be performed correctly. This tutorial describes these standards and links to more detailed scripts which will help you prepare your dataset to adhere to them if it does not already.
  - Contents: SLACK, Pixel Scale, Visibilities, Noise-Map, UV Wavelengths, Real Space Mask, Data Processing Complete, Positions (Optional), Lens Light Centre (Optional), Extra Galaxies (Optional), Mask Extra Galaxies (Optional), Info (Optional)
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Potential Correction (Interferometer)__](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/potential_correction/likelihood_function.py): This script provides a step-by-step guide of the **PyAutoLens** visibility-space potential-correction `log_likelihood_function` (the Bayesian evidence of `al.pc.FitDpsiSrcInterferometer`), which jointly inverts `Interferometer` data for a pixelized source and pixelized corrections $\delta\psi$ to the lensing potential.
  - Contents: Simplifications, Prerequisites, Dataset, Source Inversion Blocks, Dpsi Mesh, Correction Response, Joint Response, Dense Route, Sparse (w-tilde) Route, Solve, Dkappa Map, Evidence Terms, Verification, JAX / xp, Wrap Up
- [Feature: Potential Correction (Gravitational Imaging)](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/potential_correction/start_here.py): This example performs gravitational imaging on interferometer data: pixelized corrections $\delta\psi$ to the lensing potential are reconstructed jointly with the pixelized source, revealing mass structure (e.g. dark subhaloes) the smooth lens model omits, as a convergence-correction map $\delta\kappa = \frac{1}{2}\nabla^2\delta\psi$.
- [Modeling Features: Shapelets Fit (Interferometer)](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/shapelets/fit.py): A shapelet is a basis function appropriate for capturing the exponential / disk-like features of a galaxy. The `intensity` of every shapelet is solved for via linear algebra ("inversion") rather than being a free parameter of the non-linear search.
  - Contents: Advantages & Disadvantages, Positive Negative Solver, Model, Mask, Dataset, Basis, Fit, Intensities, Visualization, Wrap Up
- [Modeling Features: Shapelets (Interferometer)](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/shapelets/modeling.py): A shapelet is a basis function appropriate for capturing the exponential / disk-like features of a galaxy. It has been employed in many strong lensing studies to model the light of the lensed source galaxy, because it can represent features of disky star-forming galaxies that a single Sersic function cannot.
  - Contents: Advantages & Disadvantages, NUFFT (nufftax), Positive Negative Solver, Model, Mask, Dataset, Over Sampling, Search, Analysis, VRAM, Run Time, Result, Wrap Up
- [Subhalo Detection: Start Here](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/subhalo/detect/start_here.py): Strong gravitational lenses can be used to detect the presence of small-scale dark matter (DM) subhalos. This occurs when the DM subhalo overlaps the lensed source emission, and therefore gravitationally perturbs the observed image of the lensed source galaxy.
  - Contents: SLaM Pipelines, Grid Search, Pixelized Source, Model, SOURCE LP PIPELINE, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 1, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 2, MASS TOTAL PIPELINE, Two Datasets, Sparse Operators, Settings, Settings AutoFit, Redshifts, Mesh Shape, SLaM Pipeline
- [start_here](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/subhalo/sensitivity/start_here.py): (no summary in script docstring)
- [Simulator: Subhalo](scripts/interferometer/features/advanced/subhalo/simulator.py): This script simulates `Interferometer` data of a 'galaxy-scale' strong lens where:
  - Contents: Dataset Paths, Simulate, Ray Tracing, Output, Visualize, Tracer json
- [Data Preparation: Datacube](scripts/interferometer/features/datacube/data_preparation.py): Most users come to datacube modeling with a single 4D FITS file from CASA, with shape ``(n_pol, n_chan, n_vis, 2)`` — for example, an ALMA observation of a CO emission line might be ``(2, 34, 16984, 2)``: two polarisations, 34 spectral channels, ~17k visibilities per channel, real/imag.
  - Contents: What ALMA Gives You, Polarisation Handling, Canonical 3D Shape, Shared vs Per-Channel uv_wavelengths / noise_map, 3D-FITS Loader, Worked Example
- [Modeling: Datacube — Delaunay Source](scripts/interferometer/features/datacube/delaunay.py): This script fits a datacube — a list of `Interferometer` channels — with a single shared lens model and a per-channel **Delaunay-pixelized** source reconstruction. It is the Delaunay sibling of `modeling.py`, which fits the same cube with a `RectangularAdaptDensity` mesh.
  - Contents: Mask, Dataset, Dataset Auto-Simulation, Dataset Loading, Sparse Operators, Positions, Settings, Image Mesh, Edge Zeroing, Adapt Images, Model, Per-Channel Analyses, FactorGraph, Search, Model Fit, Wrap Up
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Datacube__](scripts/interferometer/features/datacube/likelihood_function.py): This script provides a step-by-step guide of the **PyAutoLens** `log_likelihood_function` used to fit a **datacube** — a list of N per-channel `Interferometer` objects sharing a single lens model — with a per-channel pixelized source reconstruction (specifically a `RectangularAdaptDensity` mesh and `Constant` regularization scheme).
  - Contents: Comparison, Simplifications, Prerequisites, Mesh Shape, Mask, Dataset, Lens Galaxy, Source Galaxy Pixelization and Regularization, One Channel Walkthrough, Across All Channels, Fit, Lens Modeling, Log Likelihood Function: Source Code Speed Up, Wrap Up
- [Modeling: Datacube](scripts/interferometer/features/datacube/modeling.py): This script fits a list of `Interferometer` channels — a "datacube" — with a single shared lens model and a per-channel pixelized source reconstruction. Each channel is an independent `Interferometer` dataset; the `af.FactorGraphModel` ties them together by feeding the same lens parameters into every channel's `AnalysisInterferometer.log_likelihood_function` and summing the per-channel log-evidences.
  - Contents: Mask, Dataset, Dataset Auto-Simulation, Dataset Loading, Sparse Operators, Settings, Mesh Shape, Model, Per-Channel Analyses, FactorGraph, Search, Model Fit, Wrap Up
- [Modeling: Datacube — Parametric Source](scripts/interferometer/features/datacube/modeling_parametric.py): This script fits a datacube — a list of `Interferometer` channels — with a single shared lens model and a **parametric** source (`al.lp.Sersic`) whose morphology is shared across channels and whose `intensity` varies channel-to-channel. It is the parametric-fit sibling of `modeling.py`, which fits the same cube with a pixelized source instead.
  - Contents: Mask, Dataset, Dataset Auto-Simulation, Dataset Loading, Positions, Settings, Model, Per-Channel Analyses, FactorGraph, Search, Model Fit, Wrap Up
- [Simulator: Datacube](scripts/interferometer/features/datacube/simulator.py): This script simulates an ALMA-style spectral-line `Interferometer` datacube of a 'galaxy-scale' strong lens where:
  - Contents: Cube Configuration, Dataset Paths, uv_wavelengths, Real-Space Grid, Lens Galaxy, Per-Channel Source, Per-Channel Simulate, 3D-FITS Cube, 4D CASA-like Cube, Multiple Images, Cube Summary, Cube Overview Plot, Spectrum Plot
- [Start Here: Datacube](scripts/interferometer/features/datacube/start_here.py): A datacube is a stack of interferometer observations of the same lens taken across many spectral channels — for example, an ALMA observation of a CO emission line in a high-redshift lensed galaxy, where each channel records visibilities at a slightly different frequency. The lens galaxy is the same in every channel, but the source's emission-line morphology varies across the cube: bright in channels close to the line peak, faint in channels at the line wings, and shifting in shape if the source has internal velocity structure.
  - Contents: JAX, Imports, Mask, Dataset, Dataset Auto-Simulation, Dataset Loading, Sparse Operators, Positions, Settings, Mesh Shape, Model, Per-Channel Analyses, FactorGraph, Search, Model Fit, Result, Wrap Up
- [Modeling Features: Extra Galaxies](scripts/interferometer/features/extra_galaxies/modeling.py): There may be extra galaxies nearby the lens and source galaxies, whose mass may contribute to the ray-tracing and lens model.
  - Contents: Data Preparation, Mask, Dataset, Extra Galaxies Dataset, Extra Galaxies Centres, Model, Extra Galaxies Model, VRAM, Run Time, Result, Scaling Relations, Wrap Up
- [Simulator: Extra Galaxies](scripts/interferometer/features/extra_galaxies/simulator.py): There may be extra galaxies nearby the lens and source galaxies, whose mass may contribute to the ray-tracing and lens model.
  - Contents: Model, Other Scripts, Dataset Paths, Simulate, Galaxies, Extra Galaxies, Output, Visualize, Tracer json, Multiple Images
- [Extra Galaxies: SLaM](scripts/interferometer/features/extra_galaxies/slam.py): This script provides an example of the Source, (Lens) Light, and Mass (SLaM) pipelines for fitting a lens model where extra galaxies surrounding the lens are included in the lens model.
  - Contents: Prerequisites, Group SLaM, This Script, SOURCE LP PIPELINE, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 1, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 2, MASS TOTAL PIPELINE, Extra Galaxies Centres, Two Datasets, Sparse Operators, Settings, Settings AutoFit, Redshifts, Mesh Shape, Extra Galaxies, SLaM Pipeline, Output
- [Modeling Features: Linear Light Profiles Fit (Interferometer)](scripts/interferometer/features/linear_light_profiles/fit.py): A "linear light profile" is a variant of a standard light profile where the `intensity` parameter is solved for via linear algebra every time the model is fitted to the data. This uses a process called an "inversion" and it always computes the `intensity` values that give the best fit to the data (e.g. maximize the likelihood) given the light profile's other parameters.
  - Contents: Advantages & Disadvantages, Positive Only Solver, Model, Mask, Dataset, Fit, Intensities, Visualization, Wrap Up
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Linear Light Profile (Interferometer)__](scripts/interferometer/features/linear_light_profiles/likelihood_function.py): This script provides a step-by-step guide of the `log_likelihood_function` which is used to fit `Interferometer` data with a linear light profile (e.g. a linear `SersicCore` source).
  - Contents: Prerequisites, Mask, Dataset, Lens Galaxy, Source Galaxy Linear Light Profile, Internal Intensity, Ray Tracing, Source Image (Internal), Mapping Matrix, Transformed Mapping Matrix ($f$), Data Vector (D), Curvature Matrix (F), Reconstruction (Positive-Negative), Reconstruction (Positive Only), Visibilities Reconstruction, Likelihood Function, Chi Squared, Noise Normalization Term, Calculate The Log Likelihood, Fit, Lens Modeling, Wrap Up
- [Modeling Features: Linear Light Profiles (Interferometer)](scripts/interferometer/features/linear_light_profiles/modeling.py): A "linear light profile" is a variant of a standard light profile where the `intensity` parameter is solved for via linear algebra every time the model is fitted to the data. This uses a process called an "inversion" and it always computes the `intensity` values that give the best fit to the data (e.g. maximize the likelihood) given the light profile's other parameters.
  - Contents: Advantages & Disadvantages, NUFFT (nufftax), Positive Only Solver, Model, Mask, Dataset, Over Sampling, Search, Analysis, VRAM, Run Time, Result, Intensities, Visualization, Max Likelihood Inversion, Linear Objects (Internal Source Code), Wrap Up
- [Linear Light Profiles: SLaM (Interferometer)](scripts/interferometer/features/linear_light_profiles/slam.py): This script provides an example of the Source, (Lens) Light, and Mass (SLaM) pipelines for `Interferometer` data, using a **linear light profile** in the SOURCE LP stage instead of a Multi-Gaussian Expansion (MGE).
  - Contents: Prerequisites, SOURCE LP PIPELINE, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 1, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 2, MASS TOTAL PIPELINE, Two Datasets, Sparse Operators, Settings, Settings AutoFit, Redshifts, Mesh Shape, SLaM Pipeline
- [Modeling Features: Multi Gaussian Expansion Fit (Interferometer)](scripts/interferometer/features/multi_gaussian_expansion/fit.py): A multi-Gaussian expansion (MGE) decomposes a galaxy's light into ~15-100 Gaussians, where the `intensity` of every Gaussian is solved for via linear algebra using a process called an "inversion".
  - Contents: Advantages & Disadvantages, Positive Only Solver, Model, Mask, Dataset, Basis, Fit, Intensities, Visualization, Wrap Up
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Multi Gaussian Expansion (Interferometer)__](scripts/interferometer/features/multi_gaussian_expansion/likelihood_function.py): This script provides a step-by-step guide of the `log_likelihood_function` which is used to fit `Interferometer` data with a multi-Gaussian expansion (MGE) source: a `Basis` of many linear `Gaussian` profiles whose `intensity` values are solved for analytically via a linear inversion.
  - Contents: Prerequisites, Mask, Dataset, Lens Galaxy, Source Galaxy MGE Basis, Ray Tracing, Mapping Matrix, Transformed Mapping Matrix ($f$), Data Vector (D), Curvature Matrix (F), Reconstruction (Positive-Negative), Reconstruction (Positive Only), Visibilities Reconstruction, Likelihood Function, Chi Squared, Noise Normalization Term, Calculate The Log Likelihood, Fit, Lens Modeling, Wrap Up
- [Modeling Features: Multi Gaussian Expansion (Interferometer)](scripts/interferometer/features/multi_gaussian_expansion/modeling.py): A multi-Gaussian expansion (MGE) decomposes a galaxy's light into ~15-100 Gaussians, where the `intensity` of every Gaussian is solved for via linear algebra using a process called an "inversion" (see the `linear_light_profiles` feature for a full description of this).
  - Contents: Advantages & Disadvantages, NUFFT (nufftax), Positive Only Solver, Model, Mask, Dataset, Over Sampling, Search, Analysis, VRAM, Run Time, Result, Wrap Up
- [Multi Gaussian Expansion: SLaM (Interferometer)](scripts/interferometer/features/multi_gaussian_expansion/slam.py): This script provides an example of the Source, (Lens) Light, and Mass (SLaM) pipelines for `Interferometer` data, using a **multi-Gaussian expansion (MGE)** for the source galaxy in the SOURCE LP stage.
  - Contents: Prerequisites, SOURCE LP PIPELINE, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 1, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 2, MASS TOTAL PIPELINE, Two Datasets, Sparse Operators, Settings, Settings AutoFit, Redshifts, Mesh Shape, SLaM Pipeline
- [Pixelization: Delaunay](scripts/interferometer/features/pixelization/delaunay.py): The majority of pixelized source reconstructions in the workspace use a rectangular mesh to reconstruct the source's surface brightness.
  - Contents: Image Mesh, Edge Zeroing, Fit, Model, VRAM, Adaptive Delaunay, SLaM Pipelines, SOURCE LP PIPELINE, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 1, SOURCE PIX PIPELINE 2, MASS TOTAL PIPELINE, Settings AutoFit, Redshifts, SLaM Pipeline, Prerequisites, Likelihood Function, Mask, Dataset, Source Galaxy Pixelization and Regularization, Source Pixel Centre Calculation, Ray Tracing, Border Relocation, Delaunay Mesh, Interpolation, Lens Modeling, Wrap Up
- [Features: Pixelization](scripts/interferometer/features/pixelization/fit.py): A pixelization reconstructs the source's light using a pixel-grid, which is regularized using a prior that forces the solution to have a degree of smoothness.
  - Contents: CPU Users, Advantages & Disadvantages, Positive Only Solver, Mask, Dataset, Sparse Operators, Settings, Over Sampling, Mesh Shape, Edge Zeroing, Pixelization, Fit, Wrap Up, Linear Objects, Grids, Reconstruction, Mapped Reconstructed Images, Simulated Interferometer
- [__Log Likelihood Function: Pixelization__](scripts/interferometer/features/pixelization/likelihood_function.py): This script provides a step-by-step guide of the **PyAutoLens** `log_likelihood_function` which is used to fit `Interferometer` data with an inversion (specifically a `RectangularUniform` mesh and `Constant` regularization scheme`).
  - Contents: Simplifications, Prerequisites, Mesh Shape, Edge Zeroing, Mask, Dataset, Over Sampling, Masked Image Grid, Lens Galaxy, Source Galaxy Pixelization and Regularization, Ray Tracing, Border Relocation, Source Pixel Centre Calculation, Interpolation, Mapper, Alternative Meshes, Mapping Matrix, Visibilities Reconstruction, Likelihood Function, Chi Squared, Regularization Term, Complexity Terms, Noise Normalization Term, Calculate The Log Likelihood, Fit, Lens Modeling, Wrap Up
- [Pixelization: Many Visibilities Preparation](scripts/interferometer/features/pixelization/many_visibilities_preparation.py): To perform many visibility modeling, a matrix called `nufft_precision_operator` is created and used, which encodes information and symmetries into the Fourier transform operation performed when modeling interferometer datasets, in a way that exploits the sparsity of the pixelized source reconstructions and means a very small amount of memory or VRAM is used.
  - Contents: High Resolution Dataset, Profiling Dataset, Curvature Preload, Curvature Preload Output, Wrap Up
- [Features: Pixelization](scripts/interferometer/features/pixelization/modeling.py): A pixelization reconstructs the source galaxy’s light on a grid of pixels, which is regularized using a prior that enforces a degree of smoothness in the solution.
  - Contents: CPU Users, Advantages & Disadvantages, Positive Only Solver, Model, High Resolution Dataset, Mask, Dataset, Sparse Operators, Settings, Over Sampling, Mesh Shape, Edge Zeroing, Search, Position Likelihood, Brief Description, Analysis, VRAM, Run Time, Result, Result Use, Wrap Up, Chaining, HowToLens
- [Pixelization: SLaM](scripts/interferometer/features/pixelization/slam.py): This script provides an example of the Source, (Lens) Light, and Mass (SLaM) pipelines for pixelized source modeling.
